watches.name: Mastercraft J3
watches.description: The Minase Mastercraft J3 reinterprets the iconic M3 in a more refined, contemporary and compact 37mm silhouette. Hand-finished in Japan using the signature Sallaz polishing technique , it combines distortion-free mirror surfaces, sharp edges and elegance in a fascinating expression of Japanese minimalism. Powered by the reliable Miyota 90S5 automatic movement , the J3 offers exceptional craftsmanship, versatility and everyday wearability — available in three sand-textured dial colors and multiple interchangeable strap options. A true handcrafted timepiece from Japan, where beauty lives in the finest details. The Essence of Japanese Watchmaking The Minase Mastercraft J3 marks a new chapter in Minase’s pursuit of contemporary Japanese watchmaking. Inspired by the original M3 — one of the brand’s earliest expressions of “ultimate simplicity” — the J3 refines this philosophy into a more elegant, slimmer and more versatile form. Reduced to 37mm in diameter and only 9.9mm thick , the J3 preserves the distinctive aesthetic of the M3 while offering a more compact and universally wearable profile. A Tribute to Japanese Craftsmanship Like all Minase timepieces, the J3 is handcrafted in Japan with uncompromising attention to detail. Its stainless steel case is meticulously hand-finished using the renowned Sallaz polishing technique , producing flawless mirror surfaces and razor-sharp transitions — a signature of Minase’s artisanal identity. Its cushion-shaped case frames a perfectly round dial opening, evoking the timeless elegance of 1970s design while remaining unmistakably modern. A New Movement, A New Era For the first time in the history of the J3 lineage, Minase introduces a Japanese automatic movement : the Miyota 90S5 . Beating at 28,800 vibrations per hour , this proven calibre offers: 42-hour power reserve 24 jewels High reliability and precision Slim architecture for enhanced comfort Three Light Sand Dial Variations The Mastercraft J3 is available in three refined dial colors: White Sand Beige Sand Black Sand Each dial is designed to create subtle depth and shifting light reflections depending on the angle and environment. Sharp-cut hands and luminous indexes ensure clarity in every condition. Personalize Your J3 Thanks to its one-touch quick-change system , the J3 adapts effortlessly to your style. Available with: Stainless steel bracelet Embossed calf leather straps Crocodile-pattern calf leather straps Rubber straps From classic elegance to sporty versatility, the J3 evolves with you. watches.name: Pocket Watch
watches.description: Minase pocket watch is a luxury timepiece crafted to order in stainless steel or 18K gold, featuring a hand-made maki-e lacquer dial. The caseback and bow are forged from traditional Tamahagane steel. Available with Asagimadara or Phoenix designs, it reflects refined Japanese craftsmanship and heritage. Japanese Pocket Watch – Maki-e Art Lacquer Dial in Stainless Steel or 18K Gold This exclusive high-end pocket watch showcases traditional Japanese craftsmanship and fine watchmaking. Produced strictly on order, it is available in stainless steel or 18K gold and features a hand-crafted maki-e lacquer dial. Each piece reflects precision, Japanese heritage and artisanal excellence. Design and Craftsmanship Designed to embody Japanese cultural aesthetics, this pocket watch translates traditional craftsmanship into refined horological form. It highlights attention to detail, balance, and a deep appreciation for materials, textures, and finishing. Case, Materials, and Finishing The twelve-sided case is crafted in stainless steel or 18K gold and finished using the Sallaz polishing technique, known for its distortion-free mirror surfaces. Both the bow and caseback are made from Tamahagane steel, a traditional high-carbon material historically used in Japanese sword-making. Over time, this steel develops a natural black patina through controlled oxidation. This stable and protective layer evolves gradually, deepening in tone over decades and giving each piece a distinctive character. Handcrafted Maki-e Dial Each dial is created using the traditional Wajima maki-e art lacquer technique. The process begins with a brass base that is heat-treated, polished, and lacquered. Designs are then hand-painted in lacquer, and fine powders of gold, silver, and pigments are applied before drying. This meticulous process takes several months and reflects centuries of refined Japanese craftsmanship. Dial Variations Asagimadara Dial Inspired by the migratory Asagimadara butterfly, this design symbolizes travel, seasonal change, and long-distance connection. The white wing patterns are created using the rankaku technique, where crushed quail eggshell fragments are carefully applied to the surface. Subtle square motifs evoke distant city lights, suggesting a connection between human presence and nature. Phoenix Dial The Phoenix dial represents transformation, resilience, and renewal. The mythical bird is depicted in flight with intricate detailing, including fine elements not visible to the naked eye. The final stage involves the precise hand-painting of the eye, completing the composition. Traditional Materials and Techniques The use of Tamahagane steel connects the piece to Japanese sword-making heritage. Produced in a traditional clay furnace and refined through repeated forging, this material is valued for its purity and durability. Its evolving patina adds depth and individuality over time. Accessories and Presentation The pocket watch is accompanied by a handcrafted wooden stand produced by a local artisan. The stand is individually lacquered and features a stainless steel ornament with Sallaz polishing, echoing the multi-sided geometry of the case. Included accessories: Leather pouch Two braided cords of different lengths, traditionally crafted in Asakusa, Tokyo Hand-made presentation box in Akita cedar wood

watches.description: Divido Urushi Makie Rubber’s dial in handmade in Japan with urushi tree laquer, paint and silver particles. Divido Urushi Makie With the shibo urushi technique, Minase pays tribute to one of Japan’s finest traditional crafts. Urushi laquer is mixed with paint and egg white. This gives the mixture a viscous consistency and allows the artist to play with the puddle-like color spots. Divido is the only round model in Minase collection. It is unique in terms of design and displays a high level of craftsmanship. Divido steel case is made of 28 pieces and constructed following the principle of the Japanese 3-dimentional puzzle. Through a revolutionary approach in watchmaking, the dial seems to be floating inside the case, almost suspended below the box-type sapphire window, and this is no optical illusion. Indeed, there is physical space between the case and the edges of the dial, which is only fixed by four tiny screws on the corners, enabling light to flood in from all sides on the hand-painted dial. Another special feature that meets the eye is the date window displaying the date preceding and following the current “D-day” with a little arrow pointing to the current date. What is Urushi Laquer ? Urushi is a special lacquer fabricated from the sap of the Urushi tree, which is native to Japan, China, and Korea. Lacquer sap (which happens to have some pretty nasty toxic qualities in its “raw” state) is frequently used as a lacquer in Japan because of its very resistant properties. Indeed, it contains a resin that becomes very hard, durable, and plastic-like when exposed to moisture and air. Owing to its potential toxicity, it is not the easiest or most forgiving substance to work with. Shibo Urushi hand-made dials After blending and straining the Urushi, the brass base dial is painted with a first layer of lacquer. Urushi lacquer is applied with a brush to the dial. Traditional Urushi brushes were made out of human hair because its texture was found to be just right. It is hard to find this kind of brush today even among traditional artisans. They mostly use brushes with mice or cats hair. As the urushi lacquer hardens, it absorbs moisture from the air which makes the dial perpetually shiny and slick. It isn’t really useful for a dial that’s inside a watch case, but the Urushi lacquer also withstands erosion from water, acids, alcohol and changes in temperature. For Divido Shibo Urushi dials, Hakose mixes urushi laquer with color and egg whites. It makes a special and viscous structure that enable the artist to play with the motives of color. More than a round watch Minase Divido Shibo Urushi is an exciting mix of angles and edges. The name Divido comes from the lost language of Esperanto and means Divided. And the word takes sense while watching at the case side which is joined sharply in the middle with inwards razor-sharp brushed bevels. The case of the Divido is constructed from eight parts. Yet if you look at the sides, there is something strong, powerful and virile. The finishing of the sides was inspired by the Katana, the famous samurai sword. Horizon Rubber HORIZON is the thinnest and most delicate model within the four collections offered by Minase. As the name suggests, the singular design of the Horizon watch was inspired by the harmonious, smooth horizon line. This design cue led to both the case and bracelet (or strap) to seemingly appear on a single plane. The curved shape of the case and the integration of the bracelet or the leather strap make Horizon very comfortable to wear. Its shape fits perfectly, even on small wrists. In addition, the Horizon’s thick sapphire crystal has been cut and polished from the front to the back. The result is a dome reminiscent of the water’s surface. With the Horizon Rubber, Minase wanted to create a sober watch that would pay tribute to their beautiful country. Japan is an island, so wherever you go, however different the region may look, if you walk to the shore, you’ll find that horizon line over the ocean. Minase likes the idea that when you look so far away, the ocean always looks calm, and that’s what they did with the Horizon. From the top, the overall watch looks calm and peaceful. On the other hand, seen from the sides, the watch becomes strong, powerful and virile. With its polished sides surrounding a brushed concave central part, its finish is reminiscent of the Katana, the famous samurai sword. A special feature that meets the eye is the date window displaying the date preceding and following the current “D-day” with a little arrow pointing to the current date. Handmade in Japan, these exceptional timepieces are meticulously crafted by skilled watchmakers who pour their expertise and passion into every intricate detail. A true testament to the art of watchmaking, each Divido Steel watch is skillfully hand-polished, resulting in a flawless and mirror-like finish. This dedication to perfection is evident in the smooth curves and refined lines that characterize these timepieces, creating a sense of understated sophistication. The Divido Steel collection offers a choice between a sturdy steel bracelet or a comfortable rubber band, allowing for versatility and personalization. With the steel bracelet, you can exude a sense of classic refinement, while the rubber band offers a sporty and dynamic appeal. Whichever option you choose, you can be confident that it perfectly complements the overall design and enhances the wearer’s style. Minase’s attention to detail and commitment to excellence are evident in every aspect of the Divido Steel collection. From the precision-engineered movement to the exquisite dial designs, each watch is a testament to the brand’s dedication to creating timepieces of unparalleled quality and sophistication. Indulge in the elegance and precision of a Minase Divido Steel watch, a masterpiece that transcends time and showcases the pinnacle of Japanese watchmaking excellence. watches.name: Divido Rubber
watches.description: Divido rubber Divido is the only round model in Minase collection. It is unique in terms of design and displays a high level of craftsmanship. Divido steel case is made of 28 pieces and constructed following the principle of the Japanese 3-dimentional puzzle. Through a revolutionary approach in watchmaking, the dial seems to be floating inside the case, almost suspended below the box-type sapphire window, and this is no optical illusion. Indeed, there is physical space between the case and the edges of the dial, which is only fixed by four tiny screws on the corners, enabling light to flood in from all sides on the hand-painted dial. Another special feature that meets the eye is the date window displaying the date preceding and following the current “D-day” with a little arrow pointing to the current date. More than a round watch Minase Divido rubber is an exciting mix of angles and edges. The name Divido comes from the lost language of Esperanto and means Divided. And the word takes sense while watching at the case side which is joined sharply in the middle with inwards razor-sharp brushed bevels. The case of the Divido is constructed from eight parts. It follows the Japanese HiZ principle of being able to dismantle and repair any single constituent part. The movement is encapsuled in a sort of a case, the upper part acting as a dial. On top of it comes an index ring and the whole is screwed inside the “outer” case which is composed of an upper and a lower part. This ensemble is attached together by the lugs, each being composed of two parts screwed together. Handmade in Japan As every Minase watch, the Divido rubber Collection is manufactured in Japan. All Minase timepieces bear the registered label “HiZ“ , a concept inspired by the Japanese words Hizu (exceptional) and Hi Izuru Kuni (Land of the rising sun). The products labelled HiZ are unique with innovative features such as the “case in case” structure, the extraordinary Sallaz finish and the construction principle “MORE” (Minase Original Rebuild Equation). Mechanical movement Minase’s KT7002 movement is based on the Swiss ETA 2892/A2 ébauches. This high-end execution displays hand-finished surfaces with perlage, blue screws, bridges with diamond polished bevels and a main plate and bridges in black “or”. 50 hours’ power reserve. The Minase rotor was personalized for Minase and displays the brand’s drill head logo, while several openings reveal the movement underneath. This component is assembled with MPS lubrication-free bearings. With its ETACHRON regulating system, this is a very high precision execution. 21 Jewels. Frequency 28’800 vibrations/hour (4 Hz). Hand-made dials Minase dials are inspired by the principle of Suiboku-ga: “Ink and water painting”. The Suiboku-ga painter modifies the ink dilution, the brush position, the depth of the stroke and line thickness, sharpness and level of grey. Essentially, Minase has replaced the ink with a special lacquer, but held true to the same principle. This is what gives the dial such impressive depth of reflection, shadow play, and constantly changing depending on the light hitting the dial. The base is stamped copper. Customized Minase rotor. ETACHRON regulator system. MPS lubrication-free bearings. Very high precision TOP range execution. 50 hours’ power reserve. 21 Jewels. Urushi is a special lacquer fabricated from the sap of the Urushi tree, which is native to Japan, China, and Korea. Lacquer sap (which happens to have some pretty nasty toxic qualities in its “raw” state) is frequently used as a lacquer in Japan because of its very resistant properties. Indeed, it contains a resin that becomes very hard, durable, and plastic-like when exposed to moisture and air. Owing to its potential toxicity, it is not the easiest or most forgiving substance to work with. watches.name: Horizon Steel
watches.description: Horizon Steel HORIZON is the thinnest and most delicate model within the four collections offered by Minase. As the name suggests, the singular design of the Horizon watch was inspired by the harmonious, smooth horizon line. This design cue led to both the case and bracelet (or strap) to seemingly appear on a single plane. The curved shape of the case and the integration of the bracelet or the leather strap make Horizon very comfortable to wear. Its shape fits perfectly, even on small wrists. In addition, the Horizon’s thick sapphire crystal has been cut and polished from the front to the back. The result is a dome reminiscent of the water’s surface. With the Horizon steel, Minase wanted to create a sober watch that would pay tribute to their beautiful country. Japan is an island, so wherever you go, however different the region may look, if you walk to the shore, you’ll find that horizon line over the ocean. Minase likes the idea that when you look so far away, the ocean always looks calm, and that’s what they did with the Horizon. From the top, the overall watch looks calm and peaceful. On the other hand, seen from the sides, the watch becomes strong, powerful and virile. With its polished sides surrounding a brushed concave central part, its finish is reminiscent of the Katana, the famous samurai sword. A special feature that meets the eye is the date window displaying the date preceding and following the current “D-day” with a little arrow pointing to the current date. A square watch Like all Minase watches, Horizon steel’s architecture is based on an unusually high number of parts and innovative technical solutions. To perfectly fit the domed dial and crystal, the hands are delicately bent at the tip. In addition, their rotation point is at a higher level than the corners of the glass, reinforcing the doomed impression of the case. Conceived of pure, simply drawn lines inspired by a Japanese sword, the Katana, the Horizon embodies powerful calmness, just like the sea before a storm, and the strength of nature. Handmade in Japan As every Minase watch, the Horizon Steel Collection is manufactured in Japan. All Minase timepieces bear the registered label “HiZ“ , a concept inspired by the Japanese words Hizu (exceptional) and Hi Izuru Kuni (Land of the rising sun). The products labelled HiZ are unique with innovative features such as the “case in case” structure, the extraordinary Sallaz finish and the construction principle “MORE” (Minase Original Rebuild Equation). Mechanical movement Minase’s KT7002 movement is based on the Swiss ETA 2892/A2 ébauches. This high-end execution displays hand-finished surfaces with perlage, blue screws, bridges with diamond polished bevels and a main plate and bridges in black “or”. 50 hours’ power reserve. The Minase rotor was personalized for Minase and displays the brand’s drill head logo, while several openings reveal the movement underneath. This component is assembled with MPS lubrication-free bearings. With its ETACHRON regulating system, this is a very high precision execution. 21 Jewels. Frequency 28’800 vibrations/hour (4 Hz). Stainless Steel 316L Bracelet Minase uses stainless steel 316L for all of its watches. The metal is hand-polished with the Sallaz (also called sarazu) polishing technique. The artisan polish the pieces by hand for an incredible result. They spend more than 18 hours on a single case. The sallaz polishing technique only enables the craftsmen to polish flat surfaces, so they need to be very careful not to damage the case. Specifications Horizon Steel Case : Stainless steel 316L.
